summary: FirePulse AI is a global wildfire intelligence and monitoring platform that harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations. It combines satellite detections into an interactive dashboard featuring a global hotspot map, detection statistics, regional analysis, and cross-sensor relationships. By bringing observations from different satellite instruments into one analytical view, FirePulse AI helps users better understand where active-fire detections occur and how different sensors observe the same areas. The platform also communicates sensor differences, data limitations, and uncertainty to support responsible interpretation. Built using NASA FIRMS data, FirePulse AI demonstrates how satellite observations can be transformed into accessible and transparent wildfire intelligence.
details:
What FirePulse AI Does

FirePulse AI is a global wildfire intelligence and monitoring platform designed to harmonize NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations. It retrieves NASA FIRMS data and presents satellite detections through an interactive global dashboard.

Users can explore fire hotspots on a map, filter observations by satellite and geographic region, view detection statistics, compare regional activity, and examine relationships between MODIS and VIIRS detections. The platform identifies four types of detection relationships: cross-sensor, same sensor from different satellites, same satellite during the same overpass, and repeat coverage from the same satellite.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FirePulse AI makes complex satellite observations easier to explore and understand. By bringing observations from different satellite instruments into one platform, it helps users examine overlapping detections, compare sensor observations, and better understand global active-fire patterns.

Its intended impact is to support researchers, environmental analysts, emergency-management stakeholders, and the public with accessible and transparent satellite-based wildfire information.

Technology and Tools

The platform was developed using Next.js, TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and MapLibre GL JS. NASA FIRMS provides the active-fire observations through its API. Next.js Route Handlers manage server-side data retrieval and processing, while Vercel hosts the application. Python was also used for supporting scientific analysis.

Creativity and Scientific Considerations

The project's creative contribution is its interactive approach to harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS observations while preserving their sensor and satellite identities. It considers differences in spatial resolution, temporal sampling, overlapping observations, and detection uncertainty.

FirePulse AI uses a defined temporal matching window and nominal pixel-footprint assumptions to group related detections. These groups represent analytical relationships, not confirmed unique wildfire incidents. Active-fire detections are not treated as confirmed fires, and the platform does not claim to predict wildfires.

Scientific transparency, data limitations, accessibility, and responsible interpretation were considered throughout development.
